./dev notes/history/odo customization ideas.md:10:Exactly — as a developer you have that freedom with Odoo Community Edition. Here’s how it works in practice:✅ What You Can DoClone the GitHub repo: The source code is open under LGPL v3, so you can fork it, extend modules, and build new ones.Customize for Ethiopia: Add Amharic language packs, local accounting rules, tax structures, and workflows specific to Ethiopian corporate ecosystems.Brand under your domain: You can rebrand the UI, host it on your servers or cloud, and deliver it under your own SaaS brand.Offer SaaS or perpetual licenses:SaaS: Monthly/annual subscription fees for hosted access.Perpetual: One-time license fee plus optional support/maintenance.Sell services: Beyond the software, you can charge for implementation, training, and ongoing support.⚠️ Important ConsiderationsLicense compliance: LGPL v3 allows commercial use, but if you modify core Odoo modules, you must release those changes under the same license. Custom modules you build separately can remain proprietary.Trademark rules: You cannot market your product as “Odoo” unless you comply with Odoo S.A.’s trademark policy. Instead, you brand it under your own name/domain.Enterprise features: Some advanced modules (mobile apps, studio, advanced accounting) are Enterprise-only. You can replicate them yourself, but you cannot redistribute Enterprise code.Hosting & scaling: Running SaaS means you’ll need infrastructure (servers, backups, security, uptime guarantees).🌍 Ethiopian ContextMany local firms (construction, consultancy, fintech) adopt Community Edition first, customized with Amharic language and Ethiopian tax/accounting rules. Developers often package these as localized ERP solutions under their own brand, charging either subscription or one-time fees.👉 In short: Yes, you can fork, localize, brand, and commercialize Odoo Community Edition — provided you respect LGPL licensing and Odoo’s trademark rules.Would you like me to break down the legal obligations under LGPL v3 so you know exactly what you must release vs what you can keep proprietary?

## Recommendations

- Files with embedded tokens: redact and remove from tracked history; rotate any external credentials immediately.
- service-account.json and similarly named files: treat as sensitive, move to secure vault and rotate keys.
- Backups (zip/tar/bak): inspect contents; if they contain secrets, remove from repo and rotate affected credentials.
- For any external platform (GitHub, Vercel, Hugging Face, Firebase), coordinate rotation steps before deleting live keys.
